cases.rationale: Appendix11 §1(a)(2) permits the second-level form; other policy families and operator exceptions remain incompletely researched.

Appendix11 §1(a)(1) describes the historical third-level form. RSEP2026013 withdrawal was approved, but reviewed primary sources give no implementation date; no current allowance or denial is invented.
Public contract formats do not establish a universal closed set because Registry Operator registration is expressly excepted, and current third-level implementation remains unresolved.

The prospective-candidate API contract requires an applicant label beneath a known delegated root. The pinned IANA inventory identifies name as the root; this input-contract failure is not a .name policy prohibition or a claim that bare-root DNS syntax is invalid.
Underscores fail the selected hostname normalization contract regardless of unresolved registry form policy.
Normalization can produce an A-label, but Appendix11 alone does not establish an adopted IDN table or complete name policy.
The A-label has the same canonical identity as its Unicode spelling; no IDN registration permission is inferred.
